articles.title: China curbs cloud SK Hynix’s NY chip plans
articles.summary: US officials have held up approval for American chipmaking equipment needed by SK Hynix to expand production in China, complicating the South Korean chipmaker's plans for new memory-chip plants in New York, according to people familiar with the matter.SK Hynix is seeking US export licenses to equip its Dalian plant, arguing that increased production there would help fund its planned US expansion. But the Commerce Department has yet to approve the new licenses, the people said.Its Solidigm unit plans to invest about $45 billion and build two NAND plants in Marcy, New York, two people said, with investment potentially reaching about $100 billion over time. NAND is memory that retains data even when power is turned off and is used for storage in data centers.Also Read | Samsung to make AMD, Nvidia chip parts at second Texas plant: ReportTRUMP ADMINISTRATION FACES POLICY DILEMMAThe negotiations raise questions about how far the Trump administration is willing to bend national security guardrails established to keep US technology from aiding China's military, in order to bring foreign investment and chipmaking onshore."Ultimately, none of this is going to go forward without a green light from the White House," said Leland Miller, a member of the US-China Economic and Security Review Commission, a bipartisan panel created by the US Congress. The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Negotiations are continuing, the people said, with approval for the Dalian expansion central to SK Hynix's plans in New York.Also Read | Japan to invest up to $21 billion in two US chip factories to be run by GlobalFoundriesCOMMERCE DEPARTMENT MEETINGS INTENSIFYExecutives from SK Hynix's US subsidiary, Solidigm, have met nearly 10 times with officials from the Commerce Department since late August, one of the people said. The company needs to ramp up production and develop more sophisticated NAND chipmaking in China to generate revenue to build a US facility and to stay competitive, the people said.In a meeting last week, Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler held to his position that the US would not allow more American chipmaking tools to upgrade or expand capacity, the person said, though the department has not formally denied a license to export American equipment to fill empty clean space in Dalian. The two sides are also negotiating a separate license for 2027 for equipment to keep up the Dalian facility, the person said.A spokesperson for the Department of Commerce did not immediately respond to a request for comment.In a statement last week, Solidigm said: "As a US-founded and headquartered company, Solidigm regularly evaluates strategic alternatives to best serve its customers and enhance its long-term competitiveness. The company is currently exploring options for building a NAND memory fab at potential locations around the world. No decision regarding any specific course of action has been made." Solidigm stuck to its statement from last week. SK Hynix did not immediately respond to a request for comment outside business hours.

articles.title: IDBI Bank Strike: What's on November 10?
articles.summary: A two-day nationwide strike by IDBI Bank officers and employees against the proposed sale of a majority stake in the lender to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings ended on Tuesday. The employees' union will decide its next course of action at a meeting on November 10 as it continues to oppose the disinvestment. The strike was called by the United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees, which is seeking to stop the proposed transaction. The union said the protest received a strong response from employees and officers across the country."The strike got a massive response from employees and officers across the country. We will decide the future course of action in our core committee meeting post Diwali on November 10 on the way to intensify struggle," United Forum of IDBI Officers and Employees convener Devidas Tuljapurkar said.Read more - Get ready to pay double for parking in Delhi: MCD plans to hike charges at 400 parking lots under GRAP-II; what two-wheeler and car owners need to knowHe added that the union would approach the United Forum of Bank Unions (UFBU) to seek wider support, including the possibility of a nationwide bank strike.IDBI Bank employees oppose proposed stake sale to FairfaxThe union has raised concerns about the valuation of the lender and the possibility of its assets and business capabilities being undervalued in the transaction."We are seriously concerned that the transaction may undervalue IDBI’s properties, institutional capabilities, customer relationships, future earnings and strategic importance," Tuljapurkar said.Read more - Rahul Gandhi vs Narendra Modi debate: RaGa asks public if they want open face-off; urges Nitin Gadkari, Yogi Adityanath & other BJP leaders to convince PMHe also called on the government to make the valuation process more transparent. The union wants the government to disclose the valuation methodology, the assumptions used, how real estate and other assets have been assessed, and the reasons for accepting the proposed sale price.Tuljapurkar said the public should have clear evidence that a national asset was not being transferred at a throwaway price. He also called for scrutiny of the proposed buyer's ownership structure, financial position, regulatory record and any substantiated controversies in its home jurisdiction.Congress calls IDBI Bank disinvestment a 'scam'The proposed sale has also drawn criticism from the Opposition. The Congress on Monday described the IDBI Bank disinvestment as a 'scam' and demanded that the government stop the sale to a foreign company and set up a Joint Parliamentary Committee (JPC) to investigate the process.Congress general secretary in-charge of communications Jairam Ramesh alleged that a foreign company was acquiring the lender using funds belonging to the bank itself."This is yet another major scam by the Modi government, which warrants an investigation. We demand that the process of selling IDBI Bank to a foreign company be halted," Ramesh said in a post on X.IDBI Bank stake sale: Government, LIC to sell 60.72% stakeThe Central government on October 14 approved the sale of a combined 60.72% stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for around Rs 53,000 crore (USD 5.5 billion).Under the proposed transaction, Fairfax will acquire the government's 30.48% stake, valued at around Rs 26,620 crore, and LIC's 30.24% holding, worth approximately Rs 26,440 crore.The Canadian billionaire Prem Watsa-led Fairfax will pay Rs 81 per share, above the benchmark fair value of Rs 75.99 determined by two independent valuation agencies.The deal, if completed, would mark one of the largest foreign investments in an Indian bank and a major step in the country's long-delayed banking privatisation programme.The Central government currently holds 45.48% of IDBI Bank, while LIC owns 49.24%. The transaction is expected to be completed by the end of the current financial year, subject to regulatory clearance from the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).How many employees does IDBI Bank have?IDBI Bank has 19,108 employees on its rolls, including 9,500 employees from Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Other Backward Classes categories.The lender also has 6,911 women employees and 884 employees with disabilities. The proposed stake sale has therefore become a major concern for the employees' union, which is seeking clarity on the transaction and its implications.Inputs from PTI

articles.summary: The pattern is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow. It reflects strong upward price movement during the session, with the price moving from the opening level toward the session high by the close. The pattern is commonly studied in technical analysis as an indicator of price momentum.
